chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah said:

A woman made a bequest to me, saying: 'One-third of my estate shall be used to pay my debt, and a portion of it for so-and-so.' I asked Ibn Abi Layl about this, and he said: 'I see nothing for her, I do not know what 'a portion' is.' Later, I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about it, and informed him of how the woman spoke and what Ibn Abi Layl said. He said: 'Ibn Abi Layl lied. She is entitled to one-tenth of the third. Indeed, Allah the Exalted commanded Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and said: 'Place upon each of those mountains a portion.' And the mountains at that time were ten, so the 'portion' is the one-tenth of the thing.'
ai.seo_question: How is an ambiguous bequest of 'a portion' interpreted in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the jurist Ibn Abi Layl’s uncertainty regarding an ambiguous bequest by linking the term 'portion' (juz') to a specific Quranic precedent. He cites the story of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in Surah Sad, where God commanded him to place 'a portion' on each of ten mountains, thereby establishing that 'a portion' in this context signifies one-tenth (ushr). This hadith is significant in Shia jurisprudence for resolving ambiguities in wills by grounding legal definitions in divine scriptural usage rather than mere linguistic convention.
